method: GitHub REST API metadata + file-tree reads + source-level reading of named documents. A repo is only credited with evidence if an artifact containing actual numbers, transcripts, or graded outcomes was read. A README table without a backing artifact is marked as such. No repository was modified.
note: Stars are a popularity signal, not an evidence signal; they are recorded for orientation only.

repos.role_separation: 10 roles (orchestrator, planner, plan_reviewer, executor, worker, code_reviewer, browser_verifier, visual_reviewer, closeout_verifier) in config/config.default.yaml with per-role capability floors and preferred seeds
evidence_paths: docs/benchmarks/issue-494-evidence.md (two live isolated runs, receipts, token counts)
catalog/trust-baseline.yaml (maintainer trust grants citing named runs)
src/office/scoring.py, src/office/adaptive.py, src/office/route_learning.py (routing + cost-to-success + local reward)
repos.cost_accounting: dispatches.money_actual / money_estimate; economics.py usage_events ledger (input/output/cache-read/cache-write, cost_kind actual|estimated-nominal|quota|unknown); routing evidence report aggregates by route
repos.grading: hidden acceptance tests, lane convergence verdicts, integration verification, find-classification; outcome_labels with a trust state that only degrades automatically
repos.why: The only one of the seven seeds that combines a real routing policy, a per-route cost ledger, a trust model that cannot be self-promoted, and readable live-run receipts. Its two live runs are the strongest external evidence that a cheap reviewer (gpt-6-luna@high) can close a real review gate.
repos.limits: The runs.db with the real outcome history is not published; the v31 evaluation harness ships without published results; the benchmark snapshot is a public prior, not a local outcome. The repo is one author's system and shares no task distribution with ours.

repos.role_separation: Architecture B: Planner, Router, Developer, Tester, Reviewer with a conditional retry loop. Architecture C adds role-specialised models (Llama-3-8B plan/review) and a 1.5B/7B/32B difficulty-tiered developer pool.
repos.cost_accounting: Total tokens, API calls per task, end-to-end wall-clock per task, retry count, escalation count, tier distribution, Radon static quality metrics
repos.grading: assertion-based HumanEval tests in a sandboxed subprocess with 5s timeout; Wilson score 95% CIs; n=164 tasks x 8 configurations
repos.why: The only controlled, ground-truth-graded comparison in the seed set that directly varies role specialisation, difficulty-tiered routing, always-largest routing, and prompting technique. It supplies the mission's central negative result with a mechanism and a number.
repos.limits: HumanEval function synthesis, not repository-scale integration. Small open models (1.5B-32B) - its 'cheap tier' is far below our cheap tier's capability. Kaggle + HuggingFace Inference API harness, so token accounting is not ours.

repos.role_separation: Not a multi-agent framework. A single-agent code-review benchmark with a 3-model LLM judge panel and a strict/lenient detection protocol.
evidence_paths: tasks/*/tests/ground_truth.json (the exact human-flagged defect: file, line, diff hunk, resolution thread)
scripts/summarize.py (detected / lenient / any, unscored trials counted as not detected)
repos.cost_accounting: none built in; the paper reports a 10% cost increase for the prompt-scaling arm
repos.grading: LLM judge panel (gpt-5.5, claude-opus-4.8, gemini-3.5-flash via copilot-cli) against human-verified ground truth; 995 Harbor tasks from 98 repositories
repos.why: The purpose-built instrument for the mission's central question. Its own README runs gpt-6-luna as the review agent, so the Luna-as-reviewer hypothesis is directly testable on it.
repos.limits: No published per-model results in the repo - the benchmark exists, the multi-model comparison has not been run publicly. Needs Docker, up to 19 GB of git history for the first task of a repository, ~650 GB for all tasks. Rebuilt from the paper's descriptions, so it is a reimplementation.

repos.role_separation: Markdown-declared agentic workflows with role-scoped graders, eval manifests, and per-agent token/cost accounting (AI credits, usage reports, grader results over OTEL).
repos.cost_accounting: yes - per-agent usage artifacts, AI-credit reporting, friction-cost measurement
repos.grading: declared eval manifests with grader results persisted to branches
repos.why: The most production-grade role/eval/cost instrumentation in the seed set, and it is worth reading as a design reference for what our own telemetry should carry. But it publishes no cross-model role comparison.
repos.limits: Implementation evidence only. No published result table comparing models by role.

repos.role_separation: factory-eval computes performance(agent, role, operation, language) from immutable local workflow history; a performance-mode scheduler consumes it through read-only functions.
evidence_paths: docs/evaluations.md (outcome taxonomy: approved / changes_requested / agent_failed / integration_conflict / cancelled / interrupted)
repos.cost_accounting: explicitly refuses to invent token or cost numbers when the CLI does not provide them; MCP transport failures are excluded from quality denominators
repos.grading: no LLM scores another LLM's output; outcome classification from review decisions and integration results
repos.why: Its outcome taxonomy and its 'MCP usage is not a quality signal' rule are directly reusable. Its refusal to invent cost numbers is the discipline the mission asks for.
repos.limits: No published outcome data; the SQLite history is local-only.

repos.role_separation: Named agents: context_retrieval_agent, write_eval_script_agent, plus repo_analysis and trajectory analysis over SWE-bench-style instances.
evidence_paths: scripts/compute_cost.py (aggregates status.json / cost.json / meta.json into total tokens, input/output tokens, elapsed seconds)
repos.cost_accounting: yes - per-run cost.json aggregated by compute_cost.py into total tokens and elapsed time
repos.grading: Fail2Pass gold/prediction validation on SWE-bench-style instances
repos.why: A published per-run cost artifact format (status.json / cost.json / meta.json) and a Fail2Pass grader we can copy for local experiments.
repos.limits: The repo is a data/evaluation pipeline; it does not compare models by role. The published paper's numbers are in the FSE'2026 paper, not in the repo.

repos.role_separation: Workflow registry plus task classes, specialists, models and a cost-aware routing policy (routing/policies.json, task-classes.json, specialists.json, route-decision.schema.json).
repos.cost_accounting: yes - a pricing module and a cost-aware policy layer
repos.why: A compact, readable reference for a cost-aware policy layer with an explicit decision schema. Useful as a shape reference only.
repos.limits: 27 files total, no recorded runs, no results.

repos.role_separation: A research corpus: 9 topology patterns, 4 design dimensions, 20+ company case studies.
evidence_paths: docs/agent-safety-cost-control.md (pricing-model comparison, per-PR cost estimates, runaway-cost incident list)
repos.cost_accounting: cited vendor pricing (Devin, Cosine, Paperclip, Stripe Minions), not measured
repos.why: Useful only as a citation index to other people's cost numbers, and as a list of runaway-cost failure modes to design guards against.
repos.limits: Every number is second-hand vendor pricing or an incident anecdote. No experiments of its own.

external_non_repo_evidence.title: (When) Should a Software Factory be Lights-off? Benchmarking Code Review Agents on Bug Detection
external_non_repo_evidence.key_numbers: 1,000 review tasks over 98 OSS repos (+800 industry); best agent claude-opus-5 + copilot-cli catches 71.9% of bugs in top-5 comments vs 47.7% for opus-4.6; exploration-nudging prompts gain up to 5.8% at 10% higher cost

external_non_repo_evidence.title: Is Agentic Code Review Helpful? Mining Developers' Feedback to CodeRabbit Reviews in the Wild
external_non_repo_evidence.key_numbers: 31,073 review/feedback pairs, 10,191 PRs, 239 repos; 36.4% accepted, 7.3% discussion, 56.3% rejected

external_non_repo_evidence.title: Sphinx: Benchmarking and Modeling for LLM-Driven Pull Request Review
external_non_repo_evidence.key_numbers: checklist-based review benchmark; up to 40% improvement in checklist coverage over baselines

external_non_repo_evidence.title: An Empirical Evaluation of Locally Deployed LLMs for Bug Detection in Python Code
external_non_repo_evidence.key_numbers: 349 BugsInPy bugs across 17 projects; ~43-45% accuracy for LLaMA 3.2 / Mistral; high proportion of partial, mis-localised responses

rejected_as_evidence.what: arXiv:2610.13668 and the other three arXiv entries
rejected_as_evidence.why_rejected: Not rejected - verified. Listed here only to note that each was fetched and its title, authors, date and abstract were read directly, not taken from a search snippet.

rejected_as_evidence.what: Auto Office's eval/v31 harness and routing-evidence-report script
rejected_as_evidence.why_rejected: Both are real machinery, but neither ships results. A benchmark catalog or an evaluation script is not proof an experiment was completed. Classified C, not A.

rejected_as_evidence.what: Auto Office's Artificial Analysis benchmark snapshot
rejected_as_evidence.why_rejected: Not rejected as a prior - it is version-pinned and citable - but it is a public benchmark with a different construct and a different harness. It never decides a local route on its own; Auto Office's own doc says local outcomes take precedence.
